NEW BUG #1 — ARBITRARY MONEY TRANSFER VOTE (bypass MaximumMoneyTransferRequest / wallet permissions)
File: Barotrauma/BarotraumaServer/ServerSource/Networking/Voting.cs
Lines 318-340, case VoteType.TransferMoney:
    bool startVote = inc.ReadBoolean();
    if (startVote)
    {
        int amount = inc.ReadInt32();
        int fromClientId = inc.ReadByte();
        int toClientId = inc.ReadByte();
        if (!ShouldRejectVote(sender, voteType))
        {
            pendingVotes.Enqueue(new TransferVote(sender,
                ConnectedClients.Find(c => c.SessionId == fromClientId),
                amount,
                ConnectedClients.Find(c => c.SessionId == toClientId)));
        }
    }
WHAT IS MISSING HERE:
  - No check amount <= ServerSettings.MaximumMoneyTransferRequest
  - No check that from = bank only when sender can manage wallets; from can be ANY player wallet
  - No check that to is sender (a normal player can set to anyone)
  - Non-manager normal player normally reaches money vote via MultiPlayerCampaign.ServerReadMoney
    (lines 1295+), which enforces the above. This Voting.ServerRead path is a second, weaker entry and
    is reachable via ClientNetSegment.Vote (GameServer.cs lines 1311/1486).
NORMAL CLIENT NEVER SENDS startVote=true for TransferMoney:
  - Barotrauma/BarotraumaClient/ClientSource/Networking/Voting.cs line ~299:
      case VoteType.TransferMoney:
          if (data is not int money) return false;
          msg.WriteBoolean(false); // not initiating a vote
          msg.WriteInt32(money);
  => a crafted client packet is the only way to execute this branch.
IMPACT:
  - Start a vote to transfer ANY amount (up to wallet balance) from Bank or another player to yourself,
    bypassing MaximumMoneyTransferRequest and the "receiver must be self" rule.
  - TransferVote.Finish (lines 51-71): fromWallet.TryDeduct(amount); toWallet?.Give(amount).
  - Can also enqueue unlimited pending TransferVotes with only ShouldRejectVote cooldown (minor queue spam).
NEW BUG #2 (minor / server robustness) — request malformed values cause index errors:
  - EventManager.ServerRead: selectedOption is inc.ReadByte(), then convAction.Options[selectedOption]
    (EventManager.cs line ~ 99). Out-of-range option (not 255) -> IndexOutOfRange.
  - Inventory.SharedRead (SharedSource/Items/Inventory.cs line ~1108): start/end are bytes with no
    clamp against capacity; receivedItemIds[i] can be OOB -> IndexOutOfRange.
  Not high value, but worth knowing for server-crash / desync fuzzing.
NEW BUG #3 (interesting, low impact): client can ChangeProperty on items they can access.
  - Item.ServerEventRead -> EventType.ChangeProperty -> ReadPropertyChange.
  - ReadPropertyChange (SharedSource/Items/Item.cs line ~3855) with inGameEditableOnly=true.
  - GetInGameEditableProperties(ignoreConditions:true) returns all ConditionallyEditable+InGameEditable.
  - Server then re-checks ConditionallyEditable.IsEditable(this).
  - ConditionType.OnlyByStatusEffectsAndNetwork returns GameMain.NetworkMember is {IsServer:true}
    (ConditionallyEditable.cs line ~65). So on a dedicated server these are editable:
        Item.DescriptionTag, ItemComponent.LockGuiFramePosition, ItemComponent.GuiFrameOffset.
  - CanClientAccess(sender) required. Impact is cosmetic-ish, but demonstrates the server trusts
    network property changes granted by an attribute intended for StatusEffects.
REJECTED candidates this wave (verified no bypass):
  - Fabricator: client sends recipeHash/amount, but CanBeFabricated checks CanAfford for RequiredMoney
    before Fabricate(); TryPurchase return value is ignored only AFTER CanAfford passed. No free craft.
  - Store: ReadPurchasedItems quantity clamped 0..100, DeliverImmediately gated, prices server-side.
  - Upgrades/item swaps: TryPurchaseUpgrade/PurchaseItemSwap called with force=false, price server-side.
  - ServerSettings.ServerRead: needs ManageSettings.
  - Event responses: TargetClients must contain sender.
  - Hull fire/water edit: needs ConsoleCommands + fire/editfire permission.
  - Inventory: accessibility check via IsInventoryAccessible + item.CanClientAccess.
  - TakeOverBot/hiring: hire charges through TryHireCharacter.
  - CircuitBox: CanAccessAndUnlocked + required items.
  - Wallet direct transfer (ServerReadMoney): amount<=0 return, from/from, manager checks + max amount.
[NEXT TARGETS]
  - Read EventManager option bounds patch / crash vector.
  - Check ServerEntityEventManager + Hull for water/fire DoS.
  - Look at Skill/stat updates over network (maybe client can send stats).
  - Examine ability/status effects triggered by items components (Terminal, CustomInterface) for

[WAVE 3 — ABILITY FLAGS verdict (+ rejection note)]
Files read: SharedSource/Enums.cs (653-725), Character.cs (6075-6120),
CharacterHealth.cs (130-155,650-690), CharacterAbilityGiveFlag.cs, CharacterAbilityModifyFlag.cs.
VERDICT: AbilityFlags are NOT directly network-writable from a client.
- enum AbilityFlags: MustWalk=0x1, ImmuneToPressure=0x2, IgnoredByEnemyAI=0x4,
  MoveNormallyWhileDragging=0x8, CanTinker=0x10, CanTinkerFabricatorsAndDeconstructors=0x20,
  TinkeringPowersDevices=0x40, GainSkillPastMaximum=0x80, RetainExperienceForNewCharacter=0x100,
  AllowSecondOrderedTarget=0x200, AlwaysStayConscious=0x400, CanNotDieToAfflictions=0x800.
- Character.AddAbilityFlag/RemoveAbilityFlag/HasAbilityFlag are plain private-field methods, no
  network serialization. Ability flags are granted by CharacterAbilityGiveFlag /
  CharacterAbilityModifyFlag (talents/abilities) and by missions/status effects.
- Server uses them in authoritative code:
  - CharacterHealth.IsUnconscious uses !HasAbilityFlag(AlwaysStayConscious)
  - CharacterHealth.KillIfOutOfVitality uses !HasAbilityFlag(CanNotDieToAfflictions)
  - Character.IsImmuneToPressure / Movement (MustWalk/MoveNormallyWhileDragging), AI targeting
    (IgnoredByEnemyAI), Repairable tinker gates, CharacterInfo skill gain.
- Since game runs these checks server-side and flags are not read from client packets, a normal
  client cannot "give itself" AlwaysStayConscious / CanNotDieToAfflictions over the wire.
- Potential avenue (not a bug): if a client can somehow grant a talent through UpdateTalents
  (requires CanManageTalents) whose ability is CharacterAbilityGiveFlag, the server itself adds it.
  That gates via CanManageTalents + viability checks, so not directly exploitable.
So AbilityFlags is a good "what actually is client-side" note, but it is NOT a free-heal-class bug.
[WAVE 19 — CROSS-VERIFY USER's "анализ 1/2" HITs AGAINST ORIGINAL SOURCE]
Context: user's Pastebin reports (NTQwFeTe / PiQQtBVP) were written against the DNSPY

VERIFIED TRUE in original:
- HIT #1 Free MedicalClinic (unchanged).
- HIT #2 SERVER_COMMAND outer permission skip:
  GameServer.cs:1739-1753. if (command==ManageRound && mpCampaign!=null) {} else if
  (command==ManageCampaign && mpCampaign!=null) {} else if (!HasPermission) return.
  So in a MultiPlayerCampaign, ManageRound/ManageCampaign reach the switch WITHOUT
  the outer HasPermission check.
  - ManageRound, end=false, continueCampaign=false, !GameStarted, !initiatedStartGame
    -> TryStartGame() with NO inner permission check (lines 1884-1893). ForceStartRound.
  - ManageRound, end=true: inner `mpCampaign == null || AllowedToManageCampaign(...ManageRound)`
    (lines 1815-1816) -> non-admin cannot end a running round, cannot wipe the session
    (mpCampaign==null path is also NOT reachable without ManageRound because the outer
    check applies then). So the "lobby campaign-wipe" claim does NOT hold for a
    non-permission client.
  - ManageRound map LoadNewLevel branch requires ManageCampaign||ManageMap
    (lines 1882/1862) -> NOT a non-perm bypass. The user's "map jump no perms" claim
    is WRONG.
  - ManageCampaign -> mpCampaign.ServerRead (line 1954). Inside ServerRead
    (MultiPlayerCampaign.cs:835+): hull/item repairs/lost shuttle have NO
    HasCampaignInteractionAvailable check (only GetBalance>=cost / TryPurchase).
    -> unprivileged client can remotely trigger these from anywhere, paying from
    their own balance (or bank if they have ManageWallets). Not free, but it is a
    "remote campaign purchase without NPC" weakness.
  - SELECTMODE/SELECTSUB cases also have no permission check in the switch
    (lines 1920-1952) -> lobby tamper, non-critical.
- HIT #3 TAKEOVERBOT:
  GameServer.cs:1583-1592. if (ServerSettings.ReplaceCostPercentage <= 0 ||
  AllowedToManageCampaign(ManageMoney) || AllowedToManageCampaign(ManageHires)).
  Original DEFAULT ReplaceCostPercentage = 100f (ServerSettings.cs:504), NOT 0.
  -> Free hire only when a server sets ReplaceCostPercentage<=0. On default servers the
  permission branch applies (cost = salary*100%, TryHireCharacter checks TryPurchase).
  Also reserve-bench takeover path (line 1611+) only checks AllowBotTakeoverOnPermadeath.
- HIT #4 ReadReadyToSpawn self-set SpectateOnly:
  GameServer.cs:1559-1564. sender.SpectateOnly = bool && (AllowSpectating||Owner);
  sender.WaitForNextRoundRespawn = bool. By design the client controls its own spectator
  flag; RespawnManager.GetClientsToRespawn skips SpectateOnly clients (RespawnManager.cs:22)
  and WaitForNextRoundRespawn can delay respawn (line 62). It is a self-service toggle,
  NOT a privilege escalation. Keep as low-value / design note.
- HIT #7 Force ReadyCheck:
  ReadyCheck.ServerRead (ServerSource/GameSession/ReadyCheck.cs:89-99) accepts
  state=Start when no active ready check -> StartReadyCheck(client.Name, client).
  No server permission check and no server cooldown. Client cooldown
  (ClientSource ReadyCheck.cs:288-297) is bypassable by a crafted packet.
  VERIFIED. Impact: spam 30s ready-check popup to all clients.
- HIT #8 SpectatingPos info leak:
  GameServer.cs:1489-1490 sets c.SpectatePos = vector with no auth. Used in
  ClientWriteIngame (2085-2110): if c.SpectatePos set, any sentient/character whose
  distance to that point is >= DisableDistance is still skipped (culling based on
  spectate point). A live client can send SpectatePos near an arbitrary area to
  receive entity/character state for it -> wallhack-ish info leak. VERIFIED.
- HIT #9 fake-item sell money dup:
  CargoManager.SellItems (ServerSource/GameSession/CargoManager.cs:28-64).
  For Origin=Character the server does NOT require the entity to exist or belong to
  the seller; if FindEntityByID(item.ID) returns null the item is still added and
  store.Balance -= / GetWallet(client).Give(itemValue) runs (lines 55-62). Gated in
  MultiPlayerCampaign.ServerRead by allowedToSellInventoryItems (line 1092/1100) plus
  store.Balance >= value -> effectively admin/self-host or AnyOneAllowedToManageCampaign.
  VERIFIED (privileged-only).
- HIT #10 join without required mods:
  ServerPeer.ReadConnectionInitializationStep, case ContentPackageOrder
  (ServerSource/Networking/Primitives/Peers/Server/ServerPeer.cs:207-208) just sets
  InitializationStep=Success. No client mod list is read or compared to
  contentPackages. VERIFIED.
- HIT #11 File exfiltration:
  FileSender.ReadFileRequest (ServerSource/Networking/FileTransfer/FileSender.cs:336).
  Submarine (382-397): name+hash lookup in SavedSubmarines, no permission check.
  CampaignSave (399-407): no permission check, StartTransfer(GameSession.DataPath).
  Mod (410-430) requires AllowModDownloads + AllPackages. VERIFIED. Default
  AllowFileTransfers=true makes CampaignSave/Submarine downloadable by any client.
REJECTED / CORRECTED in original:
- HIT #6 Fabricator free RequiredMoney: REJECTED. Shared Fabricator.cs:
  Fabricate() (367-372) re-checks CanBeFabricated(); CanBeFabricated (750-777) calls
  mpCampaign.CanAfford(RequiredMoney, GetUsingClient()) and returns false if the client

VOTING.TransferMoney — INDEPENDENT ORIGINAL FINDING (verified this wave again):
- Voting.ServerRead (ServerSource/Networking/Voting.cs:318-340). If startVote=true:
  reads amount (int), fromClientId (byte), toClientId (byte); only gate
  ShouldRejectVote (1-min cooldown). No check against MaximumMoneyTransferRequest,
  no requirement from==Bank when sender lacks ManageWallets, no requirement to==sender.
  TransferVote.Finish (lines 85-97): fromWallet.TryDeduct(amount) -> toWallet?.Give(amount)

  (ClientSource/Networking/Voting.cs:299-301 writes false).
  => crafted packet can start an arbitrary bank->self / other->self transfer vote,
  bypassing the cap. Needs the vote to pass, so not a "solo instant" exploit; still
  the same class of server-trusts-client bug as MedicalClinic. High priority to
  mention (and fix on a modded server) even though a majority vote is still required.

[WAVE 21 — HUNT #1: UNEXPLORED SERVER ITEM COMPONENTS + ENTITY EVENT BUFFER]
NEW STRONG FINDING — ServerEntityEventManager.Read unbounded msgLength (crash/DoS):
File: Barotrauma/BarotraumaServer/ServerSource/Networking/NetEntityEvent/ServerEntityEventManager.cs,
Read() lines 475-520. For each entity event the server reads:
    int msgLength = (int)msg.ReadVariableUInt32();
    ...
    byte[] temp = msg.ReadBytes(msgLength - 2);   // client-controlled size
There is NO validation that msgLength >= 2 or <= remaining packet bytes.
- If msgLength < 2 -> msgLength-2 is negative -> new byte[negative] (Overflow/ArgumentOutOfRange).
- If msgLength is large (near int.MaxValue) -> huge allocation attempt (OOM-ish).
- If entity == null, it does msg.BitPosition += msgLength * 8 (untrusted huge shift).
GameServer.ReadDataMessage wraps only dosProtection.Start(connectedClient); there is no
try/catch around ClientReadIngame -> entityEventManager.Read(inc, c) (GameServer.cs:1484).
=> Crafted EntityState packet can turn valid entityID + bogus msgLength into
exception / large allocation on the server. This is a NEW malformed/DoS vector not in
the user's three analyses. Severity: high for a malicious packet; server crash depends on
how the top-level Lidgren handler treats exceptions.
RE-READ item components in original (all small, all now logged full):
- DockingPort.ServerEventRead: only outpost auto-docking; requires AllowedToManageCampaign
  (ManageMap). Safe.
- Deconstructor.ServerEventRead: bool active, gated item.CanClientAccess(c), then SetActive.
  Safe (amounts/recipe server-side).
- Engine.ServerEventRead: ReadRangedInteger(-10,10)*10 -> -100..100; CanClientAccess. Safe.
- Pump.ServerEventRead: ReadRangedInteger(-10,10)*10, bool active; CanClientAccess. Safe.
- Reactor.ServerEventRead: autoTemp/powerOn/fission/turbine/temperatureBoost all ranged
  (RangedSingle(0,100,8) and (-Boost,+Boost,8)); CanClientAccess; blameOnBroken set for
  dangerous manual overrides (karma attribution). No money/fuel exploit.
- PowerContainer.ServerEventRead: ReadRangedInteger(0,10)/10*maxRechargeSpeed; CanClientAccess.
  Client cannot set charge/capacity/output. Safe.
- PowerDistributor.ServerEventRead: SharedEventRead; only NameChange/RatioChange;
  CanClientAccess. Safe.
- ButtonTerminal.ServerEventRead: ReadRangedInteger(0, Signals.Length-1), CanClientAccess,
  SendSignal. Safe.
- WifiComponent.ServerEventRead: Channel + 10 channelMemory all ReadRangedInteger(Min,Max);
  CanClientAccess. Safe; useful 10x synced int slots for mods.
- Wire.ServerEventRead: nodeCount = ReadByte() (no bound), lastNodePos = 2 raw floats
  (no MathUtils.IsValid/clamp); CanClientAccess. Weak point: arbitrary wire node coords /
  node truncation; wire nodes are used for rendering/link geometry, not a physical exploit
  on its own. Logged as minor.
- ConnectionPanel.ServerEventRead: CONFIRMED malformed vector. wires[] is a
  List<Wire>[Connections.Count]; it fills only i < min(Connections.Count, connectionCount).
  Later loops every i in 0..Connections.Count and does `wires[i].Contains(...)`/foreach
  -> if connectionCount < Connections.Count, wires[i] is null -> NullReferenceException.
  Gated by !Locked && !TemporarilyLocked && AllowRewiring && item.CanClientAccess(c).
  => crafted small connectionCount on an accessible unlocked panel = exception/log-spam.
- Terminal.ServerEventRead: reads string, CanClientAccess + !Readonly, truncates to
  MaxMessageLength, writes to display/signal_out. Safe (length capped).
CUSTOM INTERFACE -> POWERED (originally from analysis 3, now re-verified in original):
- Server CustomInterface.ServerEventRead reads raw strings/bools per element; no
  min/max/step enforcement; ValueChanged/TextChanged call
  SetPropertyValueToSignal -> (Shared CustomInterface.cs:296-315) item.AllPropertyObjects
  SerializableProperties[PropertyName].TrySetValue(po, element.Signal). This bypasses
  ItemComponent.AllowInGameEditing.

[WAVE 25 — ChatMessage rest, BanList, Voip]
- ChatMessage.ServerRead (rest, 140-262): normal chat uses SanitizeText + MaxLength +
  Levenshtein spam filter + ChatSpamSpeed + kick after >3 spam. Sender name comes from c.Name,
  not the packet. Order path was covered in Wave 20. No injection/trust hole (order
  identifier/wallSectionIndex OOB remain the only crash vectors there).
- BanList.ServerAdminRead (341-370): if no Ban permission it skips removeCount*4 bytes and
  returns false; if Ban permission, unban only with Unban permission. removeCount is UInt32;
  the no-permission skip does `BitPosition += (int)removeCount*4*8` without checking the
  remaining bytes -> huge removeCount can push seekPos out of range (minor malformed vector,
  only affects clients without Ban perm). Not a privilege bypass.
- VoipQueue.Read (136-175): BUFFER_COUNT(B) lengths are bytes 0..255 -> per packet the

  sent. No bounds check against remaining message length; a crafted voice packet can cause
  ReadBytes to read/allocate beyond the message (exception/log-spam) and it is the classic
  small-amplification case (max ~2KB per packet). Low severity but worth noting; Voice
  queue state can also be forced by sending a newer LatestBufferID (relatively cheap to
  invalidate the active voice windows). Marked.

[WAVE 29 — peer layer + correction of severity + more server files]
**IMPORTANT CORRECTION (Waves 26-28): NO PROCESS CRASH — only message-batch abort/DoS.**
- LidgrenServerPeer.Update (LidgrenServerPeer.cs:118-144) wraps the whole incoming-message foreach in
  `try { ... HandleDataMessage(...) } catch (Exception e) { record GA error; if(Verbose) log/throw }`.
  The inner catch at 285 only catches NetStructReadException, but ANY other exception (e.g.
  ArgumentOutOfRangeException from ReadCircuitBoxMessage, NullReferenceException from ConnectionPanel,
  KeyNotFoundException from Fabricator/EventManager, ArgumentException from VoipQueue.Read, Overflow
  from ServerEntityEventManager msgLength) propagates to the OUTER catch at line 135.
- P2PServerPeer.Update (P2PServerPeer.cs:74-113) catches all exceptions similarly.
- Net effect: one malformed packet aborts processing of the REMAINING messages in the current batch
  (all other queued data for that server tick is dropped), records an analytics error, and the server
  keeps running. This is a real DoS/desync/availability vector but NOT a process crash. It also means
  a malicious client can repeatedly force the server to drop large batches of legit messages.
**ServerPeer.UpdatePendingClient (ServerPeer.cs:258-280) — CONFIRMS max-players bypass race (analysis 3):**
- `if (connectedClients.Count >= serverSettings.MaxPlayers) RemovePendingClient(pendingClient, ServerFull);`
  -> NO `return`. If `pendingClient.InitializationStep == Success` the code still does:
     connectedClients.Add(...); pendingClients.Remove(...); callbacks.OnInitializationComplete(...).
  A client that races auth+content-order into Success can be promoted past MaxPlayers.
- Same IP/account duplicates are only checked in HandleConnection/AuthInfo; a second connection from the
  same endpoint can get its own PendingClient and reach Success -> duplicate active slot.
**LidgrenServerPeer.HandleDataMessage (220-310):**
- Pending/unauth clients sending non-init messages are removed (AuthenticationRequired). Good.
- Ban list re-checked after auth. Good.
- Outer try/catch confirms all handler exceptions are contained (see correction above).
**P2PServerPeer (1-423):** server owns only the ChildServerRelay pipe; auth is delegated to owner peer.
- HandleDataMessage reads remote init steps via ServerPeer.ReadConnectionInitializationStep, adds
  PendingClient on ConnectionStarted. Ban/Heartbeat/Disconnect handled. No extra privilege path.
- Send() refuses unauthenticated connections (only OwnerConnection or connected). Good.
**ServerSettings (server, full 1-637):**
- `ServerRead` (167-265) requires ManageSettings. Under an admin client, unknown net-property keys
  execute `incMsg.BitPosition += (int)(8*size)` (line 202) with NO bounds/cap check -> admin-only
  malformed-packet skip vector (can jump bit position past/negative before the next read).
- `ReadPerks` (133-165): if NO connected client has ManageSettings, any client can change perks

  send 255 and force 255 reads from a short message (malformed/DoS vector, caught by peer outer catch).

  controlling the character. Talent refund/update gated by CanManageTalents (self or ManageBotTalents).
- Write-side (350-832) is server->client only.
**DebugConsole (server, 2780-2832):**

**Item.ReadPropertyChange (Shared/Items/Item.cs:3855-4030) — CONFIRMED unclamped floats + NEW string[] OOM:**

[WAVE 31 — GameServer dispatch + ReadTakeOverBot + Client.TryTakeOverBot + crew/event server files]
**CONFIRMED — TAKEOVERBOT reserve-bench respawn-shuttle bypass (non-permadeath char swap):**
- GameServer.ReadTakeOverBotMessage (GameServer.cs:1569-1634): after Ironman global check and the
  "hireable character" branch (which correctly gates on ReplaceCost<=0 or ManageMoney/ManageHires),
  the **reserve-bench / new-hire branch** is:
  `if (botInfo is { Character: null } && (IsNewHire || IsOnReserveBench)) { if (IsUsingRespawnShuttle())
  SpawnAndTakeOverBotInShuttle(...) else SpawnAndTakeOverBot(...) }`.
- `IsUsingRespawnShuttle()` (3305-3308) returns true whenever `ServerSettings.UseRespawnShuttle` is on or
  RespawnManager.UsingShuttle — **it does NOT require Permadeath**.
- `SpawnAndTakeOverBotInShuttle` (1679-1712) NEVER calls `Client.TryTakeOverBot`. It directly:
  `DiscardClientCharacterData(client)`, `client.CharacterInfo = botInfo`, grants rename,
  `SpectateOnly=false`, `WaitForNextRoundRespawn=false`, `SetClientCharacterData(client)`.
  It does NOT check `Client.CharacterInfo.PermanentlyDead`, `RespawnMode.Permadeath`, or
  `ServerSettings.AllowBotTakeoverOnPermadeath`.
- Exploit: on any non-Ironman server with UseRespawnShuttle=true (or a shuttle already in use), a client
  who is ALIVE (or dead in normal respawn mode) can send ClientPacketHeader.TAKEOVERBOT with a
  reserve-bench/new-hire bot's ID. The server silently discards the player's current character data and
  reassigns them to the bot on the next respawn — a free character swap / duplicate-crew-slot abuser that
  ignores `AllowBotTakeoverOnPermadeath` and Permadeath. Non-shuttle branch still calls TryTakeOverBot
  (Permadeath + PermanentlyDead required), so only the shuttle branch is bypassed.
- `Client.TryTakeOverBot` (Client.cs:300-350) itself DOES enforce Permadeath + PermanentlyDead + IsBot, and
  never checks `AllowBotTakeoverOnPermadeath` — that flag is only checked in the "active bot" branch of
  ReadTakeOverBotMessage (line 1624). So if a server sets AllowBotTakeoverOnPermadeath=false, the
  reserve-bench branch STILL allows takeover (regardless of shuttle) as long as player was permadead —
  setting is effectively only applied to already-spawned bot characters.

[WAVE 31b — VOIP malformed-packet DoS + file-transfer confirmation]
**NEW — VOIP read has NO per-buffer bounds check (VoipQueue.Read, Shared/Networking/Voip/VoipQueue.cs:136-168):**
- On the "newer packet" path, for each of BUFFER_COUNT=8 buffers:
  `bufferLengths[i] = msg.ReadByte(); buffers[i] = msg.ReadBytes(bufferLengths[i]);`
  Each length is a raw byte 0-255; up to 8*255 = 2040 bytes are read without checking against
  `msg.LengthBits`. `MsgReader.ReadBytes` (Message.cs:427-432) allocates `new byte[numberOfBytes]` and calls
  `NetBitWriter.ReadBytes(...)`, so a short VOICE packet causes an out-of-bounds exception.
- On the discard path it also does `msg.BitPosition += len * 8` (VoipQueue.cs:165) with no bounds check.
- Dispatch: GameServer `case VOICE -> VoipServer.Read(inc, connectedClient)` (VoipServer.cs:132-146).
  Reachable by ANY connected client at any time, high-frequency unreliable packet. Exception is caught by
  the peer-layer Update try/catch, so it aborts the rest of the message batch for that tick (DoS/desync,
  not crash). Repeated VOICE packets = repeated legit-message drops. Same class as Wave-29 corrected DoS.
**FILE_REQUEST (GameServer.cs:1020-1024) — exfiltration only when AllowFileTransfers=true:**
- Dispatcher gates all FileTransferType on `ServerSettings.AllowFileTransfers`. When enabled, any client
  can send `FileTransferType.CampaignSave` (FileSender.ReadFileRequest) and the server will read and send
  the whole current campaign save file (characters, money, map progress) — no separate permission.
  Submarine/Mods are restricted to server-side knowledge; Mod requires AllowModDownloads+Ready+hash.
- `FileSender.ReadFileRequest` Data-ack branch also lets a client set `KnownReceivedOffset` arbitrarily
  (no `offset<=length` check), forcing a transfer to complete early (cancel). Minor availability vector.
**ServletRequestBackupIndices**: SendBackupIndices (GameServer.cs:1041-1051) has NO permission/time gate —
`REQUEST_BACKUP_INDICES` is always handled (line 1032-1034). Any client can ask for the save index data
(`SaveUtil.GetIndexData(savePath)`, client-supplied path) which includes backup indices, then use the
server's own save-path heuristic. Read-only information leak.
MARKED DONE: VoipServer(148), VoipServerDecoder(230), VoipQueue(172), Message.cs 415-433.
[WAVE 32 — GameServer dispatch (1-1105) + SaveUtil path/recon]
**CONFIRMED — REQUEST_BACKUP_INDICES is an unprivileged filesystem recon/read vector:**
- `GameServer.SendBackupIndices` (GameServer.cs:1041-1051): called for any connected client, no
  permission/rate gate. Client sends a path string `savePath`; server calls

[WAVE 33 — ClientReadServerCommand permission-skip refinement + CircuitBox DoS]
**CONFIRMED (refined) — SERVER_COMMAND ManageRound in campaign SKIPS the generic permission check and can
START a round without any permission (GameServer.cs:1741-1748 + 1849-1880):**
- For `command == ManageRound && mpCampaign != null`, the code "does nothing" (explicitly skips

**CONFIRMED — CIRCUITBOX packet DoS (GameServer.cs:1543-1557):**
`ReadCircuitBoxMessage` reads `NetCircuitBoxHeader` via `INetSerializableStruct.Read` (throws
NetStructReadException wrapped), but the `header.Opcode` switch is:
```
CircuitBoxOpcode.Cursor => ...,
_ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(...)
```
A regular client can send `ClientPacketHeader.CIRCUITBOX` with any opcode other than Cursor and cause an
unhandled `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` inside `ReadDataMessage`. There is no try/catch in this method;
the exception escapes to the peer-layer `Update` catch, which aborts the rest of the message batch for
that tick. Repeatable DoS/desync by any joined client.

[WAVE 34b — MultiPlayerCampaign: TryPurchase/fallback + ServerReadCrew]
- `CampaignMode.TryPurchase(client, price)`: for NON-wallet managers it only draws from the client's own
  wallet (`wallet.TryDeduct(price)`). For wallet managers (or the no-manager fallback that makes everyone
  "allowed to manage wallets") it may supplement from the campaign bank:
  `balance + Bank.Balance` (MultiPlayerCampaign.cs:1507-1537). Consequence: on a server where no premium
  client has ManageMoney connected, normal players are treated as wallet managers and can spend bank money
  on upgrades/store items. Good supporting info for the campaign shop exploit.
- `MultiPlayerCampaign.TryPurchase` uses `GetWallet(client)` => `GetWallet(...)` for campaign returns the
  Bank for everyone (see Shared/CampaignMode.cs:271-274). So when the "anyone manages" fallback is active,
  client wallet == bank.
- **ServerReadCrew (1263-1434)**: `validateHires`/`updatePending` block (1376-1418) is gated by
  `location.HireManager != null && HasCampaignInteractionAvailable(sender, InteractionType.Crew)` only —
  NOT by ManageHires. A client standing near the crew/hire NPC can:
    * `validateHires`: call `TryHireCharacter(...)` for every pending hire (charges from their own wallet
      / bank via TryPurchase).
    * `updatePending`: move any hireable character into/out of the pending list, and to active service
      if below `MaxCrewSize` — again without ManageHires.
  `fireCharacter`/`renameCharacter` ARE gated by ManageHires (rename-self by RenamingEnabled only). So the
  un-gated component is the pending-hire edit + validation.
MARKED: MultiPlayerCampaign.cs 1177-1506, 1263-1434, 1507-1537.

[WAVE 36 — Voting.ServerRead TransferMoney (original, exact code verified)]
**CONFIRMED — Voting.ServerRead TransferMoney vote bypass (server/Voting.cs:242-383 + 149-204 + 59-98):**
- `voteType = (VoteType)voteTypeByte` — casting int->enum never throws, so the try/catch is irrelevant.

    int amount = inc.ReadInt32(); int fromClientId = inc.ReadByte(); int toClientId = inc.ReadByte();

[WAVE 38 — ServerEntityEventManager (server 579) + NetEntityEventManager.Read]
**NEW — ServerEntityEventManager.Read has no bounds/consistency checks on client event lengths
(server ServerEntityEventManager.cs:475-542):**
- Client sends EntityState: `ushort firstEventID`, `byte eventCount`, then per event: `ushort entityID`.
- If the event ID is stale/out-of-order (line 497-503), server does `msg.BitPosition += msgLength * 8`
  with `msgLength = msg.ReadVariableUInt32()` **unchecked** (up to 2^32-1, and *8 can overflow int).
- If `entity == null` (line 505-518) it does the same unchecked skip.
- For a fresh event (line 526-530), the server reads `msg.ReadBytes(msgLength - 2)` directly — `msgLength`
  is client-controlled and not capped against the remaining packet length; a short packet throws
  out-of-bounds read.
- These reads are NOT wrapped in per-event try/catch (only `ReadEvent` in Update is), so exceptions escape
  to the peer outer catch -> remaining messages in the tick are dropped. Reachable by any in-game client via
  `ClientNetSegment.EntityState`.
- `BufferEvent` caps the buffered list at 512 (drops 256 when exceeded) — good, but only after parsing.
**CORRECTION to Waves 26-29**: ServerEntityEventManager.Update (159-204) wraps each `ReadEvent` in its own
try/catch, so malformed *component* events (CircuitBox `Options[selectedOption]`, ConnectionPanel, etc.)
that get as far as `ReadEvent` are logged (GA error) and dropped **per-event**, not only by the peer outer
catch. The stronger DoS vectors are reads that fail BEFORE the buffer (this `Read` method) and the command/
chat/settings handlers not covered by this per-event catch.

- `uint coalitionCount = msg.ReadVariableUInt32(); Identifier[] newCoalitionPerks = new Identifier[coalitionCount];`

  (e.g. 0x0FFFFFFF) -> `new Identifier[huge]` -> massive memory pressure / OutOfMemoryException.
  Reached via server ServerSettings.ReadPerks, whose `HasPermissionToChangePerks` only requires
  ManageSettings OR that no other connected client has ManageSettings — so on a server with no manager
  currently connected (or in PvP with no same-team manager) any client can trigger it.
- Unknown perk IDs are `continue`d, leaving default `Identifier`s in the array (array is replaced, not
  cleared) — minor state corruption only.
**CONFIRMED — AllowImmediateItemDelivery defaults to TRUE (shared ServerSettings.cs:813-818):**
`[Serialize(true,...)] public bool AllowImmediateItemDelivery`. `CampaignMode.AllowImmediateItemDelivery`
returns true by default for any client (unless the setting is explicitly off). So by default a client at
the store can buy items and have them delivered immediately; the `CargoManager.PurchaseItems` path is the
real gate (stock clamp + TryPurchase).
**Shared Client.ReadPermissions (Client.cs:234-266)**: only invoked by ManagePermissions holder;
`ReadRangedInteger(0, (int)ClientPermissions.All)` bounds the permission value, and permitted commands are
matched against existing DebugConsole commands. The catch around int->enum cast is a no-op.

[WAVE 40 — GameServer dispatch + MultiPlayerCampaign ServerRead/ServerReadMoney/ServerReadCrew + FileSender]
**GAMESERVER.READDATAMESSAGE (server GameServer.cs 824-1039) — full header dispatch read:**
- `REQUEST_BACKUP_INDICES` (case at 1032-1033) → `SendBackupIndices` (1041-1051) has **NO PERMISSION CHECK**:
  `string savePath = inc.ReadString(); SaveUtil.GetIndexData(savePath);` then sends the parsed

  `Path.GetDirectoryName(fullPath)` + `Directory.GetFiles(path, ".{baseName}*")` + `DecompressFile...`.

  directories for files matching `.{name}*` backup pattern (existence oracle), (b) force the server to

  Reachable via ClientPacketHeader.REQUEST_BACKUP_INDICES, no ManageSettings/owner requirement.

  Types: Submarine (restricted to saved sub matching name+hash), CampaignSave (any client gets the

- `EVENTMANAGER_RESPONSE` (1026-1027) → `GameSession.EventManager.ServerRead(inc, client)` — no auth check.

- `READY_CHECK` (1008-1009) → `ReadyCheck.ServerRead` — any client can start/update a 30s ready check,
  no permission/cooldown; moderate (spams all clients with reliable packets + blocks start state).
- `READY_TO_SPAWN` (1559-1567): `SpectateOnly = inc.ReadBoolean() && (AllowSpectating || owner)` — safe.
- `TAKEOVERBOT` (1569-1634): ironman + hireable gate; existing-bot branch requires `AllowBotTakeoverOnPermadeath`.
- `RESPONSE_STARTGAME` (843-855): sets ReadyToStart/AFK — any client can set AFK, only cosmetic.
- `ERROR` (1053-1150): client error report → KickClient on malformed data. Reachable; bounded by math.Min(subCount,5).

[WAVE 41 — GameServer.ServerCommand/permission fallback + ReadDataMessage header cartography]
**NEW/CONFIRMED — ClientReadServerCommand permission-gate holes (server GameServer.cs:1720-1995):**
- Top-level check at 1749 (`!sender.HasPermission(command)`) is **skipped entirely for

  `HasPermission` check.
**NEW/CONFIRMED — CampaignMode.AnyOneAllowedToManageCampaign (shared CampaignMode.cs:197-231) huge fallback:**
- single connected client (Count==1) → true;
- GameStarted && no one has the permission → true ("no-one with permissions, allow anyone to manage");
- GameStarted && someone has permission but round > 60s and that holder is dead/not InGame → true;
- not GameStarted && no one has permission → true.
- This means `AllowedToManageCampaign` (and thus `AllowedToManageWallets`, hire/money/map/reward paths,
  MultiPlayerCampaign.ServerReadMoney 1195, `ServerReadRewardDistribution` 1239, `ResetSalaries` 1255, store
  allowance paths) can return true for a **random client** when: server has 1 client, or no admin/money-holder
  is present/alive, or (once a round goes past 60s) the admin is dead/spectating. Combined with the
  SERVER_COMMAND gate skip, this is the umbrella behind several "no admin ever set permissions"
  privilege escalations.

**STRONG NEW/CONFIRMED — unknown prefab = server exception in multi-player store path (unprivileged):**

  - `ReadSoldItems` (shared MultiPlayerCampaign.cs:351) — parses `ItemPrefab.Prefabs[prefabId]` **at the very top

**CargoManager sell/money rules (server path) — verified, no duplicate sale:**
- `SellItems` (server CargoManager 28-66): `sellValues` computed for all non-null prefabs; only
  `store.Balance >= value` and `!item.Removed` gates. For Submarine origin with NullEntityID it picks the first
  matching sellable item from the sub (`GetSellableItemsFromSub` → `IsItemSellable` bounds by prefab/condition/

  sell sub items by ID/pack selection; that's the intended system though the permission `SellInventoryItems`
  plus `AllowRemoteCampaignInteractions` means a client can sell sub equipment from anywhere.
- `BuyBackSoldItems` (11-26): uses `campaign.TryPurchase(client, itemValue)` — price==0 returns true (Wave 20).
- `PurchaseItems` (299-377): price = `item.Quantity * buyValues[item.ItemPrefab]`; `TryPurchase` per item.
- **`store.Balance += itemValue`/`-= itemValue` both unbounded** — a high net worth can never be replicated,
  but store balance is used as an upper bound only; no negative-balance issue because the checks are
  `store.Balance < itemValue`.
- `UndeterminedSoldEntities` (426+) is cleared per `GetSellableItemsFromSub` call and is a client-side helper.
**GameServer.LidgrenServerPeer.Update outer catch (135-144)**: ANY exception from any data-message handler
(including all ServerRead* and SERVER_COMMAND paths) also **aborts processing the remaining incoming messages in
that batch** (the foreach is inside the try). So every exception-based DoS above also increases desync/latency,
not just a single player's kick.

[WAVE 48 — SaveUtil backup-index path traversal/parse + ServerSettings unbounded reads + Character input OOB]
**NEW HIGH — REQUEST_BACKUP_INDICES → SaveUtil.GetIndexData is an unprivileged arbitrary path scan/oracle + decompression DoS:**
- Server `GameServer.SendBackupIndices` (1041-1051) reads `savePath` from the client (ANY connected client)
  then `SaveUtil.GetIndexData(savePath)` and replies with the parsed backup list.
- `SaveUtil.GetIndexData` (943-1021) computes `path = Path.GetDirectoryName(fullPath)` and
  `fileName = Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(fullPath)` from the CLIENT STRING, then
  `Directory.GetFiles(path, $".{fileName}{BackupExtension}*", ...)` and for every match calls
  `ExtractGameSessionRootElementFromSaveFile(backupPath)` (722-760) which **decompresses the file
  (DecompressFileToStream) and byte-scans it** before returning location/level/save-time to the attacker.
- Consequences (unprivileged, no ManageSettings/Ban):
  1. Arbitrary directory enumeration/existence oracle: server will list files matching `.{name}.bak*`
     (and similar) in any path the server process can read, e.g. relative traversal / server config dirs,
     returning metadata for files that parse as Barotrauma saves.
  2. Server-side decompression + XML parse of attacker-path files = CPU/IO DoS; repeated requests amplify.
  3. Information disclosure of campaign backup metadata (location names, level type, save time) to any client.
- Only mitigation: the `FileName` search mask is prefixed with `.`, so files must match the backup naming
  convention, and `GetBackupPaths` catches exceptions (returns empty), but the scan/decompress happens anyway.
**ServerSettings.ReadExtraCargo (1368-1389)** — `count = msg.ReadUInt32(); for (i < count)` loops on a
client-controlled count with no upper bound; caps apply only AFTER each new item is found, so a malformed
packet with huge `count` either runs long (each iter reads a string) or throws OOB. ManageSettings-gated,
but the same "unchecked VUVarUInt/count" pattern as ReadPerks (Wave 39).
**Character.ServerReadInput (server CharacterNetworking.cs 189-267):**
- `inputCount = msg.ReadByte()` and the loop reads `ReadRangedInteger` + `ReadUInt16()` (+ more for Use/Grab)
  per input. No check that the remaining message actually contains `inputCount` records; a short packet with
  a large `inputCount` causes out-of-bounds read (exception → outer batch catch). Same `Character.ServerEventRead`
  `UpdateTalents` `talentCount = msg.ReadUInt16()` (313) loop `ReadUInt32` per talent is also unbounded and can
  OOB short packets. Reached only by the client controlling the character (not privileged).
- Note: `memInput` is capped at 60 (261-266), so buffering is bounded; the DoS is the OOB-read exception, not memory.
MARKED: SaveUtil 699-1021 (already partial), ServerSettings 1354-1476, CharacterNetworking 189-348.
[WAVE 49 — Item ServerEventRead ChangeProperty: unbounded string[] allocation (unprivileged OOM DoS)]
**NEW HIGH — `Item.ReadPropertyChange` string[] element: client-controlled allocation → server OOM:**
- Entry: `Item.ServerEventRead` (server Items/Item.cs 190-242) `EventType.ChangeProperty` → `ReadPropertyChange` (shared Item.cs 3855-4035) `else if (type == typeof(string[]))` at 3981-3993.
- `int arrayLength = msg.ReadInt32(); string[] val = new string[arrayLength];` — `arrayLength` is a **client-controlled int** with **no clamp** (unlike the `Editable.MaxLength` clamp used for single strings at 3910-3914).
- The only gate before allocation is `allowEditing` = `CanClientAccess(sender)`/circuit-box-unlocked + `ConditionallyEditable.IsEditable`. For any `[Editable]`/`[InGameEditable]` string[] property on an item the client can access (common item), sending `int.MaxValue` → OOM on the server; even modest huge values cause allocation churn.
- Also there is **no per-entry MaxLength** clamp for string elements (3906-3914 applies to single string only; `val[i] = msg.ReadString()` at 3987 is raw), so huge per-element strings can be set on accessible items and then **logged** at 4031 (log spam / disk growth).
- Reached by ANY client (not a permission). The outer batch catch in LidgrenServerPeer will catch the OOM? An `OutOfMemoryException` is not reliably catchable; even if caught, the allocation itself may destabilize the process. This is the strongest "any client can kill the server" item so far.
- Fix hints: clamp `arrayLength` against `EditableAttribute.MaxLength` (or a serialized safe cap, e.g. `0..64`) before `new string[...]`; clamp each `val[i]` length; cap log string.
**Other paths in the same switch (verified safe-ish):**
- `ComponentState`/`InventoryState` indices use `ReadRangedInteger(0, components.Count-1)` → safe bounds.
- `Treatment`: must `CanInteractWith(this)`, `targetCharacter != c.Character && c.Character.SelectedCharacter != targetCharacter` guard, healing cooldown → no cross-target healing.
- `Combine`: must `CanInteractWith` both this and combineTarget → no remote combine.
MARKED: shared Item 3855-4035, server Item 190-242.
[WAVE 50 — P2P MessageDefragmenter unprivileged memory exhaustion + fragment count OOB]
**NEW HIGH — Shared MessageDefragmenter.ProcessIncomingFragment (lines 11-39):**
- Entry: P2P server `P2PServerPeer.HandleDataMessage` (200-210) reads `MessageFragment` from an already-connected
  client (`IsDataFragment` branch) and feeds it to `connectedClient.Defragmenter.ProcessIncomingFragment`.
- `FragmentId` = `ushort FragmentIndex, ushort FragmentCount, ushort MessageId` — all client-supplied.
- Line 15: `partialMessages[fragment.FragmentId.MessageId] = new MessageFragment[fragment.FragmentId.FragmentCount];`
  → allocates an array of up to 65k entries per **new unique MessageId**, and `partialMessages` is never evicted
  (only removed when a *complete* message arrives, line 35).
- No cap on `partialMessages.Count`, no timeout, no fragment-count sanity check relative to real MTU/usage.
- Exploit: an authenticated but **unprivileged** client sends e.g. thousands of `IsDataFragment` packets, each
  with a distinct `MessageId` and `FragmentCount=0xFFFF` and one fragment. Server allocates and retains a
  ~65k-element array per message → server memory exhaustion (a few thousand packets → GBs). On Steam/EOS P2P
  relayed servers this is reachable from the wild. Lidgren (dedicated IP) servers don't use this path, but
  the shared code is hit by any `ChildServerRelay`/P2P game.
- Secondary: line 25 `fragment.FragmentIndex >= fragmentBuffer.Length` correctly bounds the *index*, but the
  `FragmentCount` itself is used as allocation size before any check. Also line 36 joins all fragment `Data`
  arrays; a full 65k-fragment message is ~65k * 1100 bytes ≈ 72 MB single allocation plus copy.
- Fix hints: cap `FragmentCount` (e.g. <= 256 / real max fragments from MTU), limit `partialMessages` count &
  add per-message timeout, and reject first-fragment counts that don't match a plausible size.
**P2PServerPeer.Send/paths verified (lines 307-423)**: sends only to connected/owner; no exploit.
**ChildServerRelay (shared 1-368)**: pipe frame `msgLength` is 4-byte so max ~4GB, but `Write` rejects
`>0x1fff_ffff` and `Read` yields messages per queued byte[]; no new exploit in relay itself.
MARKED: MessageFragmenter, MessageFragment, MessageDefragmenter, server P2PServerPeer, shared ChildServerRelay,
client/server ChildServerRelay partials.

[WAVE 53 — SegmentTableReader.Read: attacker-controlled tablePointer with no bounds check]
**NEW HIGH — shared SegmentTable.cs 265-324 (shared/used by server and client):**
- `SegmentTableReader<T>.Read` reads `int tablePointer = msg.ReadInt32()` (line 271) directly from the packet,
  then sets `msg.BitPosition = pointerLocation + tablePointer` (272-278) with **no check** that `tablePointer`
  is >=0 and within `msg.LengthBits`/buffer bounds.
- A malicious client can set `tablePointer` to an arbitrary large/negative value in ANY packet that uses
  `SegmentTableWriter` (e.g. `UPDATE_INGAME` / `UPDATE_LOBBY` server-side reads at GameServer:1264,1367).
  Consequences:
  1. `msg.BitPosition` is moved outside the valid message range; the subsequent `numSegments = msg.ReadUInt16()`
     and per-segment `INetSerializableStruct.Read<Segment<T>>` read at arbitrary offsets. Reading within the
     allocated buffer but past `LengthBits` yields stale memory interpreted as `(Identifier, Pointer)` tuples;
     reading past the end throws `IndexOutOfRange`/`ArgumentOutOfRange`.
  2. `numSegments` is a raw `UInt16` → up to 65535 `Segment` allocations (bounded, but combined with huge
     negative `tablePointer` the reads corrupt state and hit the outer `LidgrenServerPeer.Update` catch → the
     whole packet batch aborts → desync/latency DoS).
- The per-segment `SegmentReadMsg` constructor DOES validate `offset+lengthBits >= underlying.LengthBits`
  (151-155), but that check happens only AFTER the table was already read from an attacker-chosen offset.
- Recording: any `SegmentTableReader` consumer should validate `tablePointer >= 0 &&
  pointerLocation + tablePointer < LengthBits` (and `numSegments <= max`) BEFORE jumping.
MARKED: shared SegmentTable 1-330 (full).
[WAVE 54 — FileReceiver client validation + FileSender info-disclosure]
**Client FileReceiver (client side, 1-600):**
- `ValidateInitialData` (458-500) checks `fileSize` against a per-type cap (500 MiB mods, 50 MiB others),
  invalid filename chars, and extension (.sub/.save). This blocks classic path traversal because
  `Path.GetInvalidFileNameCharsCrossPlatform` includes `/`/`\` on Windows; on Linux `\` is not separator so
  `fileName="..\x.sub"` just writes a filename with a backslash (harmless on Linux). Reasonable, keep.
- `TransferOnSameMachine` (324-352): server tells the owner-only client a raw `filePath` and the client calls
  `OnFinished` on it — if a third-party were to spoof `OwnerConnection`, they could point the client at an
  arbitrary existing file path (the client uses `File.Exists` only). Owner-channel only; not a wild exploit.
- Data frames with arbitrary `offset` are buffered with a cap (`DataBufferSize=50`); out-of-order is handled
  safely.
**Server FileSender.ReadFileRequest (lines 336-436) — CAMPAIGN SAVE disclosure:**
- `FileTransferType.CampaignSave` (399-408): **any connected client** (no `ManageSettings`/`ManageCampaign`
  permission check) can request the campaign save file. The only gate is `ServerSettings.AllowFileTransfers`
  at GameServer.cs:1021, which is **default true** (`[Serialize(true,...)]` in ServerSettings.cs:644-649).
- Server responds by starting a transfer of `GameMain.GameSession.DataPath.LoadPath` — the full current
  campaign save, including bank/character data/faction/map state. On default public servers this lets any
  connected player download the entire campaign save (information disclosure and a basis for offline
  duplication/hacking). On a peer-hosted P2P server this goes out over the file-transfer channel too.
- `Submarine` request matches only `SavedSubmarines` (name+hash) — fine.
- `Mod` request is gated by `AllowModDownloads` + `ModSender.Ready` and matched by hash — fine.
- **Recommendation for mods/servers:** disable `AllowFileTransfers` unless sharing subs is actually needed,
  or gate `CampaignSave` behind `AllowedToManageCampaign(ManageCampaign)`.
**Server FileTransfer ack branch (347-377):** a client can set `expecting` arbitrarily → `KnownReceivedOffset
= Math.Max(expecting, ...)` can jump to `Data.Length` and finish the transfer early (ability to cancel/stop
own transfer; small DoS, no server leak). `lastSeen` is `Math.Min(SentOffset, clientVal)` so it can't force
server to skip past what it sent.
MARKED: client FileReceiver 1-600 (full); server FileSender already 1-439.

[WAVE 56 — SERVER_COMMAND ManageRound permission-skip: unprivileged round start]
**NEW HIGH — GameServer.ClientReadServerCommand (1720-1995):**
- Lines 1741-1748: for `command == ManageRound` or `Management==ManageCampaign`, the generic

[WAVE 57 — RESOLVED: AllowedToManage* definitions + AnyOneAllowedToManageCampaign fallback]
**Definitions resolved:**
- Server `CampaignMode.cs` 18-41 (BarotraumaServer/ServerSource/GameSession/GameModes):
  `AllowedToManageCampaign(client, perms)` = `client.HasPermission(perms) || client.HasPermission(ManageCampaign) || IsOwner(client) || AnyOneAllowedToManageCampaign(perms)`.
  `IsOwner(client)` = `client.Connection == GameMain.Server.OwnerConnection`.
- Client `CampaignMode.cs` 114-129 (BarotraumaClient/ClientSource/GameSession/GameModes): same logic using `GameMain.Client`.
- Shared `CampaignMode.cs` 197-231: `AnyOneAllowedToManageCampaign(perms)`:
  * if NetworkMember null -> true
  * if ConnectedClients.Count == 1 -> true
  * if GameStarted: if SOMEONE has perms -> after RoundDuration >= 60s, returns true when NO perm-holder alive+in-game (dead/incap/left). If no one has perms -> true.
  * else (not started) -> true when no perm-holder/client owner connected.
**NEW MEDIUM/HIGH (by-design admin fallback, demonstrably exploitable on public server):**
- ANY client is allowed to manage the campaign / wallets / hires / map / repairs / shuttle recovery whenever the permission holder is
  dead, incapacitated, or disconnected for >60s (or no permission holder exists on a dedicated server). Consequence on a
  public/community server: attacker can kill the owner (or wait until owner's character dies in-game), then:
  - spend the shared Bank via wallet-manage fallback (line 903 AllowedToManageWallets),
  - change map / buy items / buy repairs, purchase shuttles,
  - hire/take-over/manage crew (GameServer 1583-1584 free hire + takeover branch relies on same fallback),
  - kick/ban/start round via the ManageRound/ManageCampaign command paths.
- `Dedicated` servers with no `OwnerConnection` and no perm-holders: `AnyOneAllowedToManageCampaign` returns true while `ConnectedClients.Count==1` only; with >1 non-perm clients GameStarted false -> None(owner||perm-holder) == true -> true. So a lone first joiner (or by extension any client while no perm-holder in lobby) can manage. This is intentional anti-lockout but has no throttle/authentication beyond permissions.
MARKED: client CampaignMode.cs 1-470; shared CampaignMode.cs 1201-1757 remains for next pass (190 was the 197-231 snippet; the file's rest still unmarked).
[WAVE 58 — Fabricator free-craft nuance + EntityState unbounded length DoS]
**NEW LOW/MEDIUM (refine of user HIT #6) — Fabricator `Fabricate()` ignores `TryPurchase` result:**
- `Fabricator.Fabricate()` (Shared Fabricator.cs 376-396): when `RequiredMoney>0`, in MP campaign it calls
  `mpCampaign.TryPurchase(client, price)` and ignores the return value; in SP it calls `user.Wallet.Deduct` /
  `campaign.Bank.Deduct` without checking. However `CanBeFabricated()` (761-779) calls `mpCampaign.CanAfford(...)`
  BEFORE both `StartFabricating` and `Fabricate`, so a plainly broke player cannot even start. The remaining window is
  a TOCTOU: another purchase/spend between the last `CanBeFabricated` and the `TryPurchase` can cause fabrication to
  complete without payment. Severity: low-medium; not a clean free-craft as claimed.
- **`ServerEventRead` (server Fabricator.cs 9-32)** reads a client-supplied `recipeHash` and indexes
  `fabricationRecipes[recipeHash]` at line 30 without checking `ContainsKey`. Any client that can access a fabricator
  (Item.CanClientAccess) and sends an unknown hash triggers `KeyNotFoundException`. NOT a crash: the event is read via
  `ServerEntityEventManager.Update` which wraps `ReadEvent` in `try/catch(Exception)` (189-201), so it's just
  error/analytics noise; the sender is not kicked.
**NEW MEDIUM/HIGH — ServerEntityEventManager.Read unbounded msgLength (DoS):**
- `ServerEntityEventManager.Read` (475-541) reads `int msgLength = (int)msg.ReadVariableUInt32()` from every client
  entity event, then immediately does `msg.ReadBytes(msgLength - 2)` at line 529. There is NO upper bound check and
  NO minimum (msgLength<2 passes negative to ReadBytes -> array overflow exception; msgLength huge -> huge allocation).
  Path is `ClientReadIngame -> case EntityState -> entityEventManager.Read(inc, c)` (GameServer 1483-1484) with NO
  try/catch around it; the only protection is `LidgrenServerPeer.Update` outer catch (135-144) which catches the
  exception (but an OOM-scale allocation may still kill the process; in any case the peer receives a very large
  allocation request per event). **Any connected in-game client can repeatedly send msgLength=0xFFFFFFFE to pressure
  server memory or trigger an exception flood.** The buffer count guard (BufferEvent, >512) does not help because the
  exception happens before BufferEvent.
- Further: `Read` is also called from `ClientReadIngame` segment reader which is inside `ReadDataMessage`; no
  per-packet `NetStructReadException` catches this (those only wrap `PeerPacketHeaders`/`PeerPacketMessage` in
  `LidgrenServerPeer.HandleDataMessage`).
**LidgrenServerPeer (1-574):** authenticated flow OK; malformed handshake banned by IP (233-243); content-package-order
step (user HIT #10) is on line 386 (pendingClient.InitializationStep set without reading back ack — informational,
reuses the same InitStep enum), no per-file authorization; end-of-`HandleDataMessage` can be abused to make server
read an extra `PeerPacketMessage` after a malformed header? No — `ReadConnectionInitializationStep` handled separately.
MARKED: Fabricator.cs 1-1110; server Fabricator.cs 1-78; ServerEntityEventManager.cs 1-579; LidgrenServerPeer.cs 1-574.
[WAVE 59 — P2P/ServerPeer: ContentPackageOrder bypass + reconnect password skip]
**NEW HIGH (confirmed user HIT #10) — join without required mods:**
- `ServerPeer.ReadConnectionInitializationStep` case `ConnectionInitialization.ContentPackageOrder` (207-210) sets
  `pendingClient.InitializationStep = Success` WITHOUT reading or validating the client's mod list. The server only
  *sends* `ServerPeerContentPackageOrderPacket` (303-313); there is no check that the client acks the package set and
  no `ContentPackageOrder` response read from the client. A client only needs to send a packet whose
  `PacketHeader.IsConnectionInitializationStep` is `ContentPackageOrder` to advance to `Success`. So **a client can
  join a modded server without having the required content packages**; the server will proceed to the lobby with
  mismatched content (desync / missing item events / potential sync breakers). In stock this is blocked only by
  ModSender when `AllowModDownloads` is on (auto-download) or by the client itself; the server never rejects.
- **P2P child-server trust:** `P2PServerPeer.ProcessAuthTicket` (412-421) explicitly does nothing — "assume that
  authentication succeeded". Combined with `P2POwnerToServerHeader` trusting the endpoint forwarded by the owner
  process (128-129), the *owner* (host) process is the trust boundary; if compromise occurs there, full auth bypass.
- `P2PServerPeer.HandleDataMessage` (219-303): any remote sender can send `P2POwnerToServerHeader` with an arbitrary
  endpoint (only the owner process normally fills it), so a malicious owner-side frame is needed; not remotely
  exploitable from a client.
- `ServerPeer.ShouldAskForPassword` (399-409): `FindAndRemoveRecentlyDisconnectedConnection` skips password for
  recently disconnected connections — a reconnect convenience that could be abused if IP/account matching is weak.
MARKED: P2PServerPeer.cs 1-423; ServerPeer.cs 1-411.

[WAVE 63 — server-side deserialization + campaign store]
**HIGH — unauthenticated OOM/DoS in ServerEntityEventManager.Read (server EntityEventManager 475-541):**
- Client sends `ClientNetSegment.EntityState`; `Read` reads `msgLength = (int)msg.ReadVariableUInt32()` (line 492) with
  NO upper bound and then `byte[] temp = msg.ReadBytes(msgLength - 2)` (line 529) which allocates
  `new byte[msgLength-2]` BEFORE it validates that the remaining buffer is large enough
  (MsgReader.ReadBytes, Message.cs:427-433). A client can put e.g. 5 bytes `FF FF FF FF 0F` in an EntityState
  segment to request ~268 MB (or up to ~1-2 GB with the full varint) allocation per event, 255 events per segment
  (`eventCount = msg.ReadByte()`), repeatedly => rapid OOM / GC claw / server hang. No `AllowFileTransfers`-like guard;
  works even for a client in the lobby, no game state needed.
- The skip path `msg.BitPosition += msgLength * 8` (line 503) is also unbounded (same as the previously reported
  NetPropertyData skip in ServerSettings.ServerRead) -> arbitrary jump/negative/overflow bit offset -> subsequent
  reads throw OutOfRange inside the `SegmentTableReader` callback; the outer catch in `ReadDataMessage` (via
  `DoSProtection`) keeps a client connected.
**MEDIUM — arbitrary-path filesystem probe via REQUEST_BACKUP_INDICES (GameServer.cs 1041-1051):**
- Any connected client sends `savePath` (arbitrary string); server calls `SaveUtil.GetIndexData(savePath)` which does
  `Directory.GetFiles(path, ".{fileName}.save.bak*")` (SaveUtil.cs 943-1021) and returns each backup's savetime,
  location, level type + echoes `savePath` back to the client. No permission/pawn/round guard. This is a blind
  directory probe / metadata disclosure of server filesystem (e.g. test for existence of arbitrary directories,
  read timestamps/level info from any `.save.bak*` matching a chosen baseName).
**LOW — OWNER client can force server shutdown via `ClientNetError` (GameServer.cs 1141-1149):**
- It's intentional (owner error ends the game), but a connected client whose chosen client name/spoofed connection
  equals OwnerConnection is treated as owner; no auth is re-verified here beyond the connection object set at
  startup. (Not a new bug; documented for completeness.)
MARKED ServerEntityEventManager 1-579, GameServer 824-1150, ServerSettings 120-637, CharacterNetworking 189-348.
[WAVE 64 — campaign ServerRead / store + fabricator]
**MEDIUM/LOW — MultiPlayerCampaign.ServerRead (server campaign 835-1159 + shared ReadPurchasedItems 294-315):**
- `ReadPurchasedItems` reads `UInt16 itemCount` (max 65535) per store (storeCount is byte, max 255) and loops
  `j < itemCount`, creating `List<PurchasedItem>` entries with no cap, then `CargoManager.PurchaseItems` iterates.
  A client near a store can push a large packet to allocate tens of thousands of objects per update → CPU/memory
  DoS. In practice after the wire bytes run out the read throws (caught by LidgrenServerPeer.Update); only if the
  attacker pads the packet does the allocation happen.
- `PurchasedItem.ItemPrefab => ItemPrefab.Prefabs[ItemPrefabIdentifier]` (CargoManager.cs 21) uses dictionary
  indexer. A client can send an arbitrary/nonexistent item identifier in the same campaign message; any use of
  `.ItemPrefab` (e.g. `GetBuyValuesAtCurrentLocation` CargoManager.cs 305, store stock find 1035) throws
  KeyNotFoundException. Since the whole inbound loop is wrapped in LidgrenServerPeer.Update try/catch, this is
  error/log spam, not a crash; still reachable with zero permissions from a client standing at a store.
- Store quantity is clamped by store stock/already-purchased (973-977, 1035-1036) and `TryPurchase` charges
  `item.Quantity * buyValue`; no free-item bug found in the campaign store path. `TryPurchase(price==0)` short-circuit
  is intentional for free (`price == 0`) services; not exploitable for normal goods (buyValue > 0).
- `Map.SetLocation(currentLocIndex)` at 941 only when `Map.AllowDebugTeleport` (debug); fine.
- Upgrades purchase gated by `HasCampaignInteractionAvailable(Upgrade)` (1127-1129) + UpgradeManager billing; map
  select gated by AllowedToManageCampaign(ManageMap) (946); crew/hire gated by HasCampaignInteractionAvailable(Crew)
  (1339/1376). No permission bypass seen here.
**LOW — Fabricator.ServerEventRead (server 9-32) uses `fabricationRecipes[recipeHash]` (indexer) directly; a

[WAVE 67 — HIGH negative-transfer money printer; SegmentTable tablePointer]
**HIGH — negative TransferMoney amount = money creation (server Voting.cs 242-383 + Wallet.cs):**
- `ServerRead` for `VoteType.TransferMoney` reads `int amount` with **no sign/range check** and enqueues
  `TransferVote(sender, from, amount, to)` (line 324-332). `StartTransferVote` (GUI path) also has no check.
- `TransferVote.Finish` (lines 81-97) does `fromWallet.TryDeduct(TransferAmount)`. `Wallet.CanAfford(price) =>
  Balance >= price` and `Deduct(price) => Balance -= price` (Wallet.cs 185-205). With `price < 0`, `CanAfford` is
  always true and `Deduct(-N)` **increases** the payer's balance (clamped to `CampaignMode.MaxMoney`).
  Then `toWallet?.Give(negative)` only reduces the receiver (null-safe), so a client can repeatedly vote-transfer
  negative amounts from themselves (or the bank `from=null`) to create up to MaxMoney per vote.
- Activation requires the vote to actually run: `ServerRead` wrongly `enqueue`s directly instead of
  `StartOrEnqueueVote`, so if no vote is active the transfer sits in `pendingVotes`; an attacker can first start any
  other vote (e.g. Sub/SwitchSub) and then enqueue a transfer; when the first vote finishes, the transfer becomes
  Active. With `inGameClients.Count()==1` or a timeout+yes quorum it passes (Update line 213/228).
- Fix: reject `amount <= 0` and use `StartOrEnqueueVote`; ideally require `CanAfford` and a positive `amount`.
**LOW — SegmentTableReader.Read (SegmentTable.cs 265-324):** `tablePointer` and each segment's `Pointer` are
attacker-controlled and used as `msg.BitPosition = pointerLocation + pointer` with **no bounds check** before reading
the table. Malformed pointers read outside `LengthBits` but within the underlying buffer (stale/uninitialized bytes)
or throw OOR (caught by LidgrenServerPeer). This is the generic primitive that lets a client craft segment tables for
entity events (see the `ServerEntityEventManager.Read` huge-`msgLength` allocation in wave 63). By setting the table
to point inside its own payload, a client can drive `ReadBytes(msgLength)` allocations with attacker-picked lengths.
MARKED SegmentTable 1-330, server Voting 1-518, shared Wallet 1-237.
**Clarification:** the normal direct transfer packet IS guarded — `MultiPlayerCampaign.ServerReadMoney`
(1177-1233) rejects `Amount <= 0` and caps bank-request votes at `MaximumMoneyTransferRequest`. The vulnerable path
is only `Voting.ServerRead` (VoteType.TransferMoney), which reads the raw `int amount` and constructs `TransferVote`
without any sign/cap check. So a client can bypass the direct-transfer guard by using the vote message.

**FINDING A (HIGH) - HandleReleasedFragment (NetPeer.Fragmentation.cs 106-169):**
  Chain verified end-to-end: client Data packet with fragment bit -> NetPeer.Internal.ReceiveSocketData
  (472-590) sets msg.m_isFragment -> sender.ReceivedMessage -> channel receiver -> m_peer.ReleaseMessage
  (Internal.cs 78-94) -> HandleReleasedFragment.

    [Conditional("DEBUG")] - compiled out in release).

    of up to ~256MB per unique group id, driven purely by the client, BEFORE any plausibility check

    NEVER evicted: removed only when a group completes (line 152); no timeout (LastReceived is commented
    out!), no per-connection limit, and the outer NetConnection key is retained => a client that sends

    NetConnection alive (GC root). Verified by grep: no other writes to the dict anywhere.

**FINDING B (LOW) - NetBuffer.ReadBytes(int) (NetBuffer.Read.cs 83-91):**
  `NetException.Assert` is [Conditional("DEBUG")] => in release, `new byte[numberOfBytes]` is allocated
  before any bounds check. Any library-level call path with a client-controlled count = allocation DoS

  bits before GetString (release returns null "to protect against DDOS") => strings are safe, raw

[WAVE 76 - client peers (connect/auth) + client ServerSettings + voip writer]
ClientPeer.cs (1-255 FULL): the client-side initialization state machine.
  - Flow: AuthInfoAndVersion -> client sends ClientAuthTicketAndVersionPacket {Name, OwnerKey, AccountId,
    AuthTicket, GameVersion, Language} -> ContentPackageOrder -> client reads ServerPeerContentPackageOrderPacket

[WAVE 199 - TalentOverspendModule build-compat fix (user's workshop compile error CS1061)]
User compiled against the INSTALLED game binary (WorkshopMods/2880887340/CSharp) = a different build than
our repo source. Two compile-time hazards in the module fixed:
 1) Character.IsTalentLocked(Identifier) is public in THIS repo (Character.cs:5811, stat Locks via
    StatTypes.LockedTalents) but ABSENT in the user's game build => CS1061. Replaced with OPTIONAL
    reflection (_miIsTalentLocked, resolved in EnsureReflection; guarded call in StructurallyViable).
    Degradation is safe: the server-side IsViableTalentForCharacter enforces its own locked-talent
    check, so a missing local mirror can only make the simulator OVERESTIMATE viability; the packet
    builder's retry/stall logic absorbs that (packet sends, server skips, no progress, stall abort).
 2) TalentPrefab is INTERNAL in source (class TalentPrefab : PrefabWithUintIdentifier, static public
    field TalentPrefabs) => TalentPrefab.TalentPrefabs.Find would ALSO fail CS0122 from a mod assembly
    on this source layout. Replaced with a lazily-built Identifier->UintIdentifier map via reflection:
    enumerate (IEnumerable)TalentPrefabs, read Prefab.Identifier + PrefabWithUintIdentifier.UintIdentifier
    (both public base properties) => _uintById cache (ResolveUintIdentifiers). Never references the
    internal type at compile time.
LESSON (generalizes to all our modules): compile against the TARGET BINARY's public API, not the repo
source. Repo-fork may be newer/older than the installed game. Rule of thumb: internal-in-source types
(TalentPrefab, TalentTree, TalentSubTree, TalentOption...) and recently-added public members
(IsTalentLocked, EventManager additions) must go through reflection with graceful degradation.
Public-safe members used by the module (verified in source): Character.ClientEventWrite, nested public
UpdateTalentsEventData + EventType.MinValue/MaxValue, Info.GetTotalTalentPoints/GetUnlockedTalentsInTree/
UnlockedTalents, Job.Prefab.Identifier, GameMain.Client.CreateEntityEvent, DebugConsole.NewMessage.

[WAVE 209 - THE missing piece: blockers need FULL MAX, not Required (binary-verified)]
User field test: base rows 1-2 unlocked, chosen specialization opened, but OTHER specializations
never unlocked + stall "unlocks nothing". Root cause in shipped binary TalentTree.cs:
  TalentTreeMeetsRequirements = requiredTrees.All(HasEnoughTalents) && !blockedTrees.Any(HasAnyTalent && !HasMaxTalents)
  HasMaxTalents(subtree) = ALL stages at MaxChosenTalents.
So a blocker stops blocking only when EVERY stage of it is filled to Max (>= MaxChosenTalents),
NOT RequiredTalents. My FillStage filled to Required => chosen spec stayed "any selected && !max"
=> permanently blocked all other specializations => stall.

blocker fully maxed in its packet(s) => victims unlock in their packets => whole tree. Max-fill also
trivially satisfies HasEnoughTalents for "requires". Combined with plan-budget=Max (wave 208), the
entire job tree is now reachable regardless of real points — the whole point of the exploit.
Also explains user's "6th skill": stage Max caps are real server caps; extra points roll over to
next stages/subtrees per plan order — correct behavior, not a bug.

[WAVE 210 - hotfix: regression from wave 209 Max-fill — support talents burned the budget]

Note: stage "needs" within one packet are best-effort padding; if fewer unconfirmed exist than
Max, packet is shorter — server-side HasEnough/HasMax evaluate against packet selections UNION

[WAVE 219 - Full sell/purchase/inventory-theft audit + fallback permission bypass]
SELL SYSTEM (MultiPlayerCampaign.ServerRead -> CargoManager.SellItems):
  Client sends SoldItem { prefabId, itemId, removed, sellerId, origin } where origin =
  Character or Submarine. Server gates: AllowedToManageCampaign(sender, SellSubItems/SellInventoryItems).
  SellItems does NOT verify item ownership. Money goes to sender wallet, not item owner.
  => With permission: can sell ANY item by known ID, even from another player's inventory.
  Without permission: gated at AllowedToManageCampaign.
  SellOrigin.Submarine + NullEntityID => server picks matching prefab from sub (fail-safe vs selling
  more than exists). SellOrigin.Character or real ID => server finds by ID and removes. No ownership check.

PERMISSION FALLBACK BUG (AnyOneAllowedToManageCampaign):
  AllowedToManageCampaign = hasPermission || isOwner || AnyOneAllowedToManageCampaign
  AnyOneAllowedToManageCampaign = true when:
    a) only 1 client on server (always true for solo host), OR
    b) round duration >= 60s AND no-one with the permission is alive+in-game
  => On any server where the admin/owner disconnects (or all perm holders die),
     EVERY player can sell/purchase/map-select for 60s+ until someone relogs.
  => This is by design ("fallback") but it's the reason the sell system is exploitable
     by ANY player when the owner is absent: you inherit ALL campaign permissions.

INVENTORY THEFT: Inventory.ServerEventRead is well-defended. HandleRemoved/HandleAdded both
  check CanClientAccess per-item before dropping/adding. No bypass found.

MONEY TRANSFER: ServerReadMoney checks sender.CharacterID for self-wallet, requires
  AllowedToManageWallets (= ManageMoney perm) for bank or other-player transfers.
  MaximumMoneyTransferRequest caps vote-based bank withdrawal.

PURCHASE: PurchaseItems => TryPurchase => price==0 || TryDeduct. Price is server-computed.
  No client-controllable price vector.

NET RESULT: no clean new exploit of the UpdateTalents class. The sell system has an ownership
gap but requires permissions (which can be obtained via the fallback when admins are absent).
